card.name: Inside all-caps label warning text
card.fires_on: Short words and word endings inside ALL-CAPS label text, such as BOWEL, PATIENTS, SHOULD BE, and THE in a capitalized name. Most are in boxed warning lines.

modes.label: Caps product name
modes.description: The ending EL of BOWEL in the capitalized product name SUPREP BOWEL PREP KIT.
modes.example: Pediatric use information is approved for Braintree Laboratories, Inc.’s SUPREP BOW<<EL>> PREP KIT (sodium sulfate

modes.label: Caps warning phrases
modes.description: BE after SHOULD or CANNOT, or S ending PATIENTS, in all-caps warnings.
modes.example: IF CEFDINIR IS TO BE GIVEN TO PENICILLIN-SENSITIVE PATIENTS, CAUTION SHOULD<< BE>> EXERCISED BECAUSE CROSS-H

modes.label: Caps name in prose
modes.description: THE inside a capitalized saint's name in ordinary web text.
modes.example: He must have spent some time with Saint ANTONY<< THE>> GREAT before his death.

card.writes: It promotes single capital letters like S, A, and D, which suggests it favors short capitalized pieces continuing the caps text.
card.plain: It fires on small pieces of words in capital-letter text, like the warning lines on drug labels.
